# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `bogey docs` from tools/cli/src/commands.ts. Do not edit manually. -->

`bogey` administers an instance: things you can't do from the browser, or shouldn't be able to.
Run it as `bogey <command>` once the alias in [Getting started](../getting-started.md#a-bogey-command) is set, or `vpr bogey <command>` from the repo without it (`bogey` alone opens a menu). In the Docker image it's `bogey` already.
Commands that talk to Supabase read `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from `.env`.
At a terminal, a command asks for what its flags leave out. `--no-input` (or `BOGEY_NO_INPUT=1`) turns that off
for scripts: nothing is asked, and a command that needs an answer says which flag gives it.

The image carries the CLI too: `docker compose exec web bogey <command>`. It has no checkout, so the
commands that author Bogey (schema, themes, types, release) and the ones that control the host
(`upgrade`, `restart`, `stop`) explain what to do instead. The last column says where each one works.

| Command | What it does | Works in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`backup`](#backup) | Copy Storage files, and with a database URL its data, to a folder | checkout, container |
| [`config`](#config) | Check bogey.config.ts, and write the keys only it sets to the database | checkout, container |
| [`console`](#console) | Start the operator console on this machine (127.0.0.1 only) | checkout |
| [`db`](#db) | The schema baseline and migrations: freeze, add, status, migrate, repair | checkout; container: `status`, `migrate`, `mark-applied`, `repair` |
| [`docs`](#docs) | Regenerate the settings and CLI references, or build the wiki | checkout |
| [`doctor`](#doctor) | Check the sign-up hook, .env safety and plugin configuration | checkout, container |
| [`email`](#email) | Regenerate the fallback email templates GoTrue uses without the hook | checkout, container |
| [`event`](#event) | List, publish, delete, export or restore events | checkout, container |
| [`login`](#login) | Print a sign-in code for an account, without sending email | checkout, container |
| [`mfa`](#mfa) | Turn the authenticator-app requirement for instance admins on or off | checkout, container |
| [`org`](#org) | Set up the first organization, create others, and manage their hostnames | checkout, container |
| [`plugins`](#plugins) | List, inspect, enable, disable or scaffold plugins | checkout; container: `list`, `info`, `outdated`, `status`, `migrate`, `sql` |
| [`restart`](#restart) | Restart the app from deploy/compose.yml, or rebuild it with --build | checkout, host |
| [`stop`](#stop) | Stop the app's containers | checkout, host |
| [`queues`](#queues) | Show waiting mail and webhook deliveries | checkout, container |
| [`release`](#release) | Cut a Bogey release: bump the version, stamp the changelog, tag and push | checkout |
| [`reset`](#reset) | Factory-reset a database: dump it, confirm, then re-apply the baseline | checkout, container |
| [`seed`](#seed) | Create the demo hackathon and contest in an org | checkout, container |
| [`themes`](#themes) | Regenerate the theme list from packages/ui/src/styles/themes | checkout |
| [`types`](#types) | Regenerate packages/db's Database types (core schema only) | checkout |
| [`watch`](#watch) | Keep generated files up to date while developing | checkout |
| [`setup`](#setup) | Write .env from .env.example, then apply the schema and create the first organization | checkout; container: `--all-in-one` only |
| [`upgrade`](#upgrade) | Back up, merge upstream, install, migrate and check, in one go | checkout |

## backup

```
bogey backup [--out <dir>] [--db-url <postgres url>]

Copies every Storage object into <dir>/storage/<bucket>/... through the Storage
API (service key from .env). With a database URL (--db-url, or DATABASE_URL
from the environment or .env), also writes <dir>/data.sql: a pg_dump of the
public, auth and storage schemas' data (needs pg_dump).

To restore: apply supabase/migrations to a fresh Supabase, run data.sql with
psql (rows that already exist are skipped), then upload the storage folder.
<dir> defaults to backups/<timestamp>.

Short flags: -d --db-url, -o --out
```

## config

```
bogey config [check | apply]

Reads bogey.config.ts (or the file BOGEY_CONFIG names) and checks it against the
schema. The keys an admin can't change in the app (appUrl, network, and
security.requireAdminMfa) are written to the database by the server when it
starts; check compares them with the database .env points at, and apply writes
them now, without a restart. Keys the file leaves out keep the database's value.
```

## console

```
bogey console [--port <number>]

Starts the operator console from a checkout: a page for this machine only (127.0.0.1) that shows
doctor, migration and queue status, tails container logs, and runs this CLI's operator commands
(database, plugins, orgs, events, restart and upgrade). Its Local link carries a one-time token;
open it in a browser on this machine. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
The console is never part of the public image or the web app.
```

## db

```
bogey db <subcommand>

  bogey db url                 Print this instance's local Supabase URLs (API, Studio, DB, mail)
  bogey db studio              Open Supabase Studio in a browser
  bogey db baseline [--check]  Build supabase/migrations/20260924000000_baseline.sql from
                               supabase/schemas, after regenerating the setting
                               defaults and notification kinds (--check: fail if any is stale).
                               Once a release has shipped the baseline, only regenerates those two
  bogey db freeze <version>    Mark the baseline as shipped in <version>; from then on
                               schema changes are new migrations
  bogey db migration <name>    Add supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_<name>.sql, from
                               `supabase db diff` when a local stack is running
  bogey db status  [--db-url]  Which migrations a database has applied
  bogey db migrate [--db-url]  Apply the pending ones, oldest first, each in a transaction, then
                               those of the plugins that ship with Bogey (challenges)
  bogey db repair  [--db-url]  Bring an older database in line with supabase/schemas (below)
  bogey db mark-applied [--db-url] <version>|--all
                               Record migrations as applied without running them, for a
                               database set up manually

--db-url defaults to DATABASE_URL (from the environment or .env). status, migrate and mark-applied need psql
and use the table the Supabase CLI keeps, so `supabase db push` agrees.

Reads ports from supabase/config.toml, so these only resolve for a local
`supabase start` stack. A self-hosted deployment or Supabase Cloud has its
own Studio elsewhere (see docs/self-hosting.md).

bogey db repair [--db-url <postgres url>] [--dry-run] [--yes]

Brings a database's core schema in line with supabase/schemas, for one set up
by an older Bogey or changed manually. It reads what the database has, then:

  - creates missing tables and enum types, and adds missing columns and enum values
  - brings existing tables' check, foreign key and unique constraints in line: ones the
    schema dropped or changed are dropped before the seed rows, new ones added after. A
    check or foreign key that existing rows break holds for new rows only, with a warning
  - re-applies every function, view, trigger, policy, index, grant and cron job,
    so each matches the schema files
  - re-runs the schema's seed rows, skipping ones that already exist

It never drops a table, column or row; columns the schema doesn't know about are
listed and left alone. Everything after the enum values runs in one transaction,
so a failure changes nothing. Before the first release it also records the
baseline as applied.

--db-url defaults to DATABASE_URL (from the environment or .env); needs psql. --dry-run says what's missing
without changing anything. At a terminal it shows the plan and asks before changing anything;
--yes skips the question. Plugins' tables are theirs: bogey plugins migrate.

Short flags: -y --yes, -n --dry-run, -d --db-url, -c --check
```

## docs

```
bogey docs [--check]
bogey docs wiki --out <dir> [--repo <owner/name>]

Regenerates the references in docs/reference: settings.md from the settings registry, cli.md from
these commands, notifications.md, windows.md and permissions.md. --check fails when any is stale.

`wiki` writes docs/ as GitHub wiki pages into <dir> (a clone of the wiki
repo): one flat page per file, with links between docs pointing at pages and
links to other repo files pointing at GitHub.

Short flags: -o --out, -c --check
```

## doctor

```
bogey doctor [--remote]

Checks that this instance is wired up: bogey.config.ts reads and is valid (BOGEY_CONFIG
names another file), the sign-up hook in supabase/config.toml
(and, when GOTRUE_* variables are set, the self-hosted equivalent), .env
safety, that disabled plugins are installed, and, when DATABASE_URL is set (environment or .env),
that the database has applied every migration (needs psql). It also asks GitHub whether a
security advisory names this version (an issue) and whether a newer release is out (a note),
unless update checks are off. Exits non-zero on any issue.

  --remote   Also check the project .env points at, through its API with the service key:
             sign-ups and auto-confirm, that the schema is applied and an organization exists,
             the app address, whether the keys only bogey.config.ts sets match the database,
             and whether mail has gone through the Send Email hook. With
             SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN (a Management API token, Supabase Cloud only) it reads the
             dashboard's hook, OTP length and authenticator-app settings too.

Short flags: -r --remote
```

## email

```
bogey email templates [--check] [--name <org name>] [--out <folder>]

Bogey's default layout is packages/utils/templates/layout.html. This turns it into
packages/utils/src/layout.gen.ts (what the app and CLI import), then writes
supabase/templates/*.html from the layout and Bogey's default wording, using
GoTrue's own template variables. GoTrue sends these only when Bogey's Send Email
hook isn't set up (local `supabase start`, or self-hosted stacks pointing
GOTRUE_MAILER_TEMPLATES_* at them); with the hook, the app renders every email
from the settings instead. --check fails when a file is out of date.

GoTrue doesn't know which org an email is for, so these name one: the instance's
brand name, or --name. --out writes somewhere else (a self-hosted stack's template
folder) and skips the repo's own files and --check.

Short flags: -o --out, -c --check
```

## event

```
bogey event list [<org>]
bogey event visibility <org>/<event> draft|unlisted|public
bogey event delete <org>/<event> [--yes]
bogey event export <org>/<event> --out <folder>
bogey event import <folder> [--org <slug>] [--slug <new-slug>] [--name <name>]
                   [--starts-at <date> | --shift-days <n>] [--people]

list shows each org's events, or one org's. visibility publishes an event (public or
unlisted) or takes it back to a draft. delete removes an event with everything in it,
files included; it asks you to type the event's address, and --yes skips that for scripts.
It works even when bogey.config.ts sets events.uiDeletion to false.

export writes an event to a folder: manifest.json, one JSON file per table and the uploaded files.
import makes a new event from such a folder, in this or another instance, as a draft. Every id is new.
Without --people only the event's setup comes back (windows, divisions, prizes, forms, criteria, rounds, pages,
settings, agenda). --people also restores members (creating accounts for emails that have none), teams,
registrations, submissions and files, votes, scores, feedback, awards, results, announcements and check-ins.
Dates move with --starts-at (the event's new start) or --shift-days. Uses the service key.

Short flags: -y --yes, -o --out
```

## login

```
bogey login <email>

Prints a sign-in code for an account that already exists, without sending email.
Refuses unknown addresses (see --create).

  --create      Also create the account if there is no such user, even in an org
                that only lets invited people sign up. Off by default: a typo
                would otherwise mint a real, sign-in-able account.
  --app <url>   Where the printed sign-in link opens (default http://localhost:3000).
```

## mfa

```
bogey mfa [status | on | off]

Whether instance admins need an authenticator app before the database treats
them as admins (Instance > Settings > Accounts). It's on by default. If every
admin is locked out, `bogey mfa off` lets them back in with their email
sign-in alone; turn it back on after they've set one up in Account. Admins can't
change it in the app. When bogey.config.ts sets security.requireAdminMfa, the
server puts that value back when it next starts, so change it there too.
```

## org

```
bogey org <subcommand>

  bogey org list
  bogey org init [--org <slug> --name <name> --owner <email>] [--host <hostname>] [--demo] [--app-url <url>]
  bogey org create --org <slug> --name <name> --owner <email> [--host <hostname>]
  bogey org domain add <slug> <hostname>
  bogey org domain remove <hostname>

create makes --owner (created if needed) the org's owner, but not a platform
admin; use `bogey org init` for an instance's first org (the default org, whose
owner is a platform admin; `bogey setup` offers it too). Hostnames added here
count as verified, so hosted mode issues certificates for them.
```

## plugins

```
bogey plugins: manage plugins (packages/plugins/installed/<key>, and bundled/<key> that ship with Bogey)

  bogey plugins list              Every installed plugin and whether it's disabled
  bogey plugins search [words]    Find plugins in the libraries this instance searches
  bogey plugins add <key>[@<version>] [--yes] [--force]
                      [--require-attestation] [--no-verify]
                                  Install a plugin from a library (the newest version unless one is named)
  bogey plugins add github:<owner>/<repo>/<plugin>@<version> [same flags]
                                  Install a release from a repository, after showing what it is and its SQL;
                                  checks GitHub's attestations with gh
  bogey plugins library [list]    The libraries searched: the official one, then bogey.libraries.json's
  bogey plugins library add github:<owner>/<repo>
  bogey plugins library remove github:<owner>/<repo>
  bogey plugins schema [index|libraries]   Print the JSON Schema of a library's index.json, or of bogey.libraries.json
  bogey plugins install           Restore the plugins in bogey.plugins.lock exactly
  bogey plugins link <folder>     Develop plugins in place: point installed/ at a checkout (and give
                                  it the node_modules its plugins need)
  bogey plugins info <key>        Version, author and where it's published
  bogey plugins outdated          Ask each plugin's repository for a newer version
  bogey plugins remove <key> [--yes] [--dry-run] [--db-url]
                                  Uninstall: drop everything its migrations made, its rows in
                                  Bogey's tables and its files; also clears plugins already deleted
  bogey plugins disable <key>     Keep it installed but switch it off for this instance
  bogey plugins enable <key>      Undo disable
  bogey plugins status [key...] [--db-url]    Which plugin migrations a database has applied
  bogey plugins migrate [key...] [--db-url]   Apply pending ones in order, each in a transaction
  bogey plugins sql [key...]        Print migrations + seed.sql for psql (all enabled plugins by default)
  bogey plugins new <key> --repo=github:you/repo   Scaffold a plugin

Short flags: -y --yes, -n --dry-run, -f --force, -d --db-url
```

## restart

```
bogey restart [--build] [service...]

Restarts the app (and Caddy, if you name it) from deploy/compose.yml. With --build it
rebuilds the image first: a theme or an installed plugin is part of the build, so only a
rebuild picks it up. A change to bogey.config.ts (brand, repository, updates, security,
plugins.disabled) only needs the restart, since the app reads it when it starts. Settings
and email templates need neither; they apply as soon as they're saved.

The web app can't do this itself, on purpose: restarting a container needs control of
the host, which a public web app must never have.

Short flags: -b --build
```

## stop

```
bogey stop [--down]

Stops the containers in deploy/compose.yml. --down also removes them (volumes, and so
Caddy's certificates, are kept). Supabase runs separately and isn't touched.
```

## queues

```
bogey queues [--json]

How much mail and how many webhook deliveries are waiting, how old the oldest is, and the last
failure of each. Reads the tables with the service key.
```

## release

```
bogey release [patch | minor | major | pre | <version>] [--pre <id>]
              [--push] [--skip-checks] [--no-freeze] [--dry-run]
bogey release check <tag>
bogey release sync <tag> [--yes]

Releases Bogey from main, in order:

  1. checks the working tree is clean, you're on main, and main isn't behind origin
  2. checks CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section has something in it, and an "Upgrade notes"
     section when the database (supabase/) or the plugin API changed since the last tag
  3. runs vp check, the tests, and the baseline and docs checks (--skip-checks skips them)
  4. sets package.json's version, turns Unreleased into "## <version> (<date>)"
     under a fresh Unreleased, and on the first non-prerelease freezes the
     baseline (bogey db freeze; --no-freeze skips it)
  5. commits "[release] Bogey v<version>" and tags it v<version>
  6. pushes main and the tag to origin with --push, or asks; the tag starts
     .github/workflows/release.yml, which publishes the image and the GitHub release

patch, minor and major bump package.json's version; --pre beta makes it a
prerelease (minor --pre beta: 0.1.0 → 0.2.0-beta.0), and pre bumps the
prerelease number (0.2.0-beta.0 → 0.2.0-beta.1). Without a version it asks.

`bogey release check <tag>` checks a tag is releasable: its package.json
version and CHANGELOG.md section match (with Upgrade notes where the rule above asks). The pre-push hook and the release
workflow run it, so a mismatched tag never reaches GitHub.

`bogey release sync <tag>` compares the GitHub release's notes with that version's
CHANGELOG.md section (the local file is the source of truth) and, when they differ,
shows the difference and asks before overwriting them (--yes overwrites without asking).
It needs the gh CLI, signed in.

Short flags: -y --yes, -n --dry-run
```

## reset

```
bogey reset [--db-url <postgres url>] [--out <dir>] [--yes]

Puts a database back to factory default: every user, organization, event and row
is deleted, then the baseline in supabase/migrations is applied fresh.

First it writes a full pg_dump (custom format) to <dir>/pre-reset.dump, and stops
if that fails; a reset never runs without one. Then it asks you to type "reset".
--yes skips only that question, for scripts; the dump is still made.
<dir> defaults to backups/reset-<timestamp>. --db-url defaults to DATABASE_URL (from the environment or .env).
Needs pg_dump and psql. Storage objects are not touched.

To undo: pg_restore --clean --if-exists --no-owner -d <url> <dir>/pre-reset.dump

Short flags: -y --yes, -d --db-url, -o --out
```

## seed

```
bogey seed demo [--org <slug>]

Creates (or recreates) the demo hackathon in an org, plus each enabled plugin's
demo (a plugin provides one as `public.<key>_seed_demo(p_org uuid)` in seed.sql).
Uses the default org unless --org is given. No accounts are created.
```

## themes

```
bogey themes

Reads packages/ui/src/styles/themes/<key>.theme.css and writes the theme
imports (packages/ui/src/styles/themes.css) and the theme list
(packages/config/src/themes.gen.ts). A file's label comes from a
`/* @theme Label */` line; "default" styles :root, others :root[data-theme="<key>"].
`bogey watch --themes` keeps them up to date.
```

## types

```
bogey types [--mcp <url> | supabase gen types args...]

Regenerates packages/db/src/types/database.gen.ts, keeping only what
supabase/schemas creates (plugin tables are left out). The types describe the
schema files, not a deployment: generate them from any database that has the
current schema (bogey db repair first), and commit them. Production never runs this.

  bogey types                                    DATABASE_URL from .env (or --local without one)
  bogey types --db-url postgres://...              any database you can reach (a dev server,
                                                 a tailnet address; ?sslmode=disable without TLS)
  bogey types --project-id <ref>                 a Supabase Cloud project (SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN)
  bogey types --local                            from `supabase start` (needs Docker)
  bogey types --mcp http://localhost:8080/mcp   a self-hosted Studio MCP (SSH tunnel)

Needs the Supabase CLI (brew install supabase/tap/supabase); --local and
--db-url run it. The output is laid out with vp fmt before plugin entries are dropped.

Short flags: -d --db-url
```

## watch

```
bogey watch [--themes] [--settings] [--email]

Regenerates files derived from the repo while you work (`pnpm dev` runs it).
With no flags, runs every watcher.

  --themes    packages/ui/src/styles/themes → themes.css and @bogey/config/themes
  --settings  packages/config/src/settings.ts → SQL defaults, baseline, docs/reference
  --email     packages/utils/templates/layout.html, packages/config/src/email.ts → layout.gen.ts, supabase/templates
```

## setup

```
bogey setup [--missing-only] [--from-env]
bogey setup --all-in-one --host <host>[,<host>...] [--http] [--out <dir>] [--smtp-host ...]

Writes the root .env from .env.example, asking for each value (secrets show
as dots), then offers to apply the database schema (bogey db migrate) and to create the
first organization (bogey org init).

  --missing-only   Only ask for values .env doesn't have yet
  --from-env       Don't ask: take every value from the environment (for CI),
                   and fail when a required one is missing

--all-in-one writes the .env for deploy/all-in-one (Bogey, the Supabase services it
needs and Caddy in one compose file) and makes every secret it needs: the database
password, the JWT secret, the anon and service keys signed with it, the Realtime and
Studio keys and the Send Email hook secret. Run it again to change hosts or mail;
secrets that exist are kept.

  --host <hosts>   Where Bogey is served, comma-separated; the first is the main one
  --http           A trial without certificates: http:// everywhere
  --saml           Turn on SAML single sign-on and make its signing key
  --out <dir>      Where .env goes (default deploy/all-in-one; in the image, a mounted folder)
  --smtp-host --smtp-port --smtp-user --smtp-pass --smtp-from
                   The mail server, if you'd rather not edit .env afterwards

Short flags: -o --out
```

## upgrade

```
bogey upgrade [--to <tag> | --pre | --branch <name>] [--remote upstream]
              [--db-url <postgres url>] [--skip-backup] [--require-verified] [--dry-run]

Brings this fork up to date with Bogey, in order:

  1. checks the working tree is clean
  2. backs up Storage, and the database's data with a database URL (bogey backup)
  3. merges the latest release tag of <remote> (--to <tag> for a specific one,
     --pre to allow prereleases, --branch <name> to follow a branch instead);
     on conflicts it stops and says how to finish. For a tag it asks GitHub (gh release
     verify) whether the release is attested and says so; --require-verified refuses an
     unattested one
  4. vp install
  5. applies pending migrations with a database URL (bogey db migrate, then
     bogey plugins migrate), or says how
  6. regenerates the theme list, email templates and setting defaults
  7. bogey doctor
  8. prints the CHANGELOG entries that came in

The database URL is --db-url, else DATABASE_URL from the environment or .env.

After resolving a merge and committing it, run it again to continue. --dry-run
prints the steps without doing anything.

Short flags: -n --dry-run, -d --db-url, -r --remote
```
